# Luis Miguel Díaz Pichardo {.unlisted}

## PhD Researcher in Robotics and Mechatronics {.unlisted}

My current PhD research focuses on autonomous navigation for unmanned ground vehicles operating in unknown, unstructured and difficult terrain.

I work across terrain perception, 2.5D mapping, planning and sampling-based predictive control, while remaining broadly interested in robotics, autonomous systems and related engineering problems.

## Accepted at IROS 2026
:::

::: {.featured-paper}
::: {.featured-paper-copy}
<span class="status-badge">IROS 2026 · ACCEPTED</span>

### Observation-Conditioned Rollout Allocation for Sampling Model Predictive Control on Myopic Egocentric Elevation Maps

This work studies how to allocate predictive-control rollouts according to the robot's current local observation. The objective is to use a limited sampling budget more effectively while navigating with only a myopic 2.5D elevation map.

[View the IROS 2026 project](research/iros2026/){.btn .btn-light}
:::

::: {.featured-paper-meta}
**Platform**<br>
Car-like unmanned ground vehicle

**Representation**<br>
Egocentric 2.5D elevation maps

**Control**<br>
Sampling-based model predictive control

**Validation**<br>
Simulation and real-world experiments
:::
:::

<p class="eyebrow">CURRENT PHD RESEARCH</p>

## Autonomous UGV navigation in unstructured terrain
:::

:::: {.research-grid}
::: {.research-card}
### Terrain representation

Elevation, slope, roughness, clearance, unknown space and vehicle-footprint constraints represented in local and global terrain maps.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Planning and guidance

Terrain-aware global routes, local guidance and reactive decisions for partially observable environments.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Predictive control

Real-time MPPI methods that evaluate feasible motion while preserving explicit control and safety constraints.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Real-robot deployment

ROS 2 pipelines integrating RGB-D cameras, LiDAR, embedded GPU computation and field experiments.
:::
::::

::: {.home-closing}
## Research developed from simulation to real robots

My PhD currently investigates how UGVs can navigate autonomously in unknown outdoor terrain, with particular interest in field and search-and-rescue robotics.

[Read the complete research overview](research/){.btn .btn-primary}
:::
